title: gui-player configuration
description: Describes every entry of `settings` in gui-player.json (which lives next to the executable and is created with the defaults when missing). The file holds the current values as a list of {key, value}; this schema holds everything else about them. settingType USER entries are shown in Tools > Settings, built from controlType and values; SYSTEM entries are state the application keeps for itself (window, dividers). values.minPoints (dividers only) is a floor in points that is never broken, whatever the percentages of minValue and maxValue say. values.defaultValue is used when an entry is missing or invalid and by 'Restore default'; it may be absent for SYSTEM entries with no meaningful default. Also in the file, outside `settings`: `lastOpened`, the history of opened compositions (most recent first, absolute paths as {key, value}).

maxLastOpened.settingDescription: Maximum number of files kept in File > Open recent.

path.settingDescription: Folder where the open and export file dialogs start.

windowMaximized.settingDescription: Whether the window was left maximized. When false it opens restored, at windowX/windowY with windowWidth x windowHeight.

windowX.settingDescription: Horizontal position of the restored window. Without it (or without windowY) the system places the window.

windowY.settingDescription: Vertical position of the restored window. See windowX.

windowWidth.settingDescription: Width of the restored window, in points.

windowHeight.settingDescription: Height of the restored window, in points.

tracksWidthPercent.settingDescription: Share of the window's width taken by the tracks (C); the tabs and properties column (A + B) gets the rest. Position of the vertical divider. minValue and maxValue are how far it can be dragged, in percent; minPoints is the least either side may have, in points, and it always wins over the percentages.

tabsHeightPercent.settingDescription: Share of the height of the left column taken by the tabs (A); the properties (B) get the rest. Position of the horizontal divider. minValue and maxValue are how far it can be dragged, in percent; minPoints is the least either side may have, in points, and it always wins over the percentages.
